scenarios.requirement: Period Policy Form Exposes Only Live Fields, Described Honestly
scenarios.scenario: Each working field's copy matches its real behavior

outcome.text: each of the eleven retained fields describes its real current effect: - `autoCreatePeriods` — the period-creator scheduler creates the next period when the schedule advances - `periodLengthDays` — the scheduler spans each created period this many days - `defaultDeadlineDays` — the scheduler sets the deadline this many days after period start - `workingDays` — feeds the deadline (business-date) calculation - `gracePeriodHours` — submissions within this many hours past the deadline are always accepted - `allowLateSubmissions` — governs ONLY whether submissions are accepted after the grace window (off → rejected after grace; on → still accepted) - `autoPublishAfterDeadline` — the hourly auto-publisher publishes any still-draft period once `deadline + grace` has passed; it reads this flag independently, with NO "requires Auto-create periods" dependency - `autoArchiveWeeksAfterPublish` — the auto-archiver archives a published period this many weeks after publish (0 = never) - `deadlineTime` — configured `HH:MM` in `defaultTimezone`, applied with minute precision by both manual creation and scheduled auto-creation - `allowReopenAfterPublish` — the reopen request-path gate rejects reopen when off - `reopenWindowHours` — the reopen gate rejects reopen beyond this many hours after publish

proofs.detail: The source outcome bundles eleven backend effects: period creation/length/deadline/working-day calculation, grace and late-submission acceptance, auto-publish, auto-archive, deadline timezone precision, and reopen/window gates; these effects cannot be established by rendered copy.

proofs.consequence: The Settings → Periods copy accurately describes each retained field's current behavior.

scenarios.requirement: Policy activation and derived rule status are atomic
scenarios.scenario: a policy cross-pairs kind and audience

outcome.text: a direct database write is rejected by the canonical CHECK Saving `ReminderPolicy.active` and cascading the corresponding active/paused status to its derived rules MUST occur in one database transaction. A committed inactive policy MUST never coexist with an active derived rule visible to due queries or the execution-creation guard. Rule materialization MUST serialize on each policy row with `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`, then re-read and revalidate its active flag and validity window before creating or updating a rule. Policy writes and materialization therefore share the same row-lock boundary. Admin recovery MUST use that same policy-first, derived-rules-second lock order. Explicit schedule reconciliation MUST recheck the latest rule version only after acquiring the policy and report locks, then reconcile it according to the immutable version contract above. Missing-rule recovery MUST instead preserve any existing rule version and create only absent policy-report pairs.

Rule materialization MUST serialize on each policy row with `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`, then re-read and revalidate its active flag and validity window before creating or updating a rule. Policy writes and materialization therefore share the same row-lock boundary. Admin recovery MUST use that same policy-first, derived-rules-second lock order. Explicit schedule reconciliation MUST recheck the latest rule version only after acquiring the policy and report locks, then reconcile it according to the immutable version contract above. Missing-rule recovery MUST instead preserve any existing rule version and create only absent policy-report pairs.
